roads.name: County Line Road;East Palmer Divide Avenue
words: Properly twisty: 16 curves in 2.8 miles, about 6 a mile.
Tight and technical: most curves turn on a radius under 130 ft.
From 7,178 to 7,430 ft, with 517 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 55 mph limit its corners still ask for about 2.14 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this assumes 55 mph.

roads.name: North Lariat Drive
words: Properly twisty: 29 curves in 4.5 miles, about 6 a mile.
The 2.0 miles at the west end are tamer, with about 4 side roads a mile.
From 6,005 to 6,465 ft, with 918 ft of up and down along the way.
14 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
